mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as elevated interest rates compress equity valuations by increasing the discount rate applied to future cash flows.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day S&P 500 returns is positive or insignificant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 320 signals accelerating inflation, which triggers equity market sell-offs due to reduced real returns and increased risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 320, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is not negative (p>0.05) in the triggered regime.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and low housing starts (HOUST < 1500) signals an overheating labor market and weak housing demand, which together indicate an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (UNRATE < 4.0 AND HOUST < 1500) occurs in more than 40% of cases where the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by GDP growth above 23500 billion and industrial production above 103.0), the economy is overheating, leading to a higher risk of recession and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 40% of instances where GDPC1 > 23500 AND INDPRO > 103.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as strong industrial output signals robust economic growth and improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and 5-day S&P 500 returns is negative or insignificant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals a weakening labor market, which triggers equity market risk aversion and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5, or the correlation between UNRATE and 60-day returns is not negative (p>0.05) in the triggered regime.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low housing starts (HOUST < 1500) and low residential sales (RSAFS < 720000) signals a weak housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (HOUST < 1500 AND RSAFS < 720000) occurs in more than 40% of cases where the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as elevated unemployment signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings potential.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE and 5-day S&P 500 returns is positive or insignificant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
